feedback.problem:
Given that $f(x)=|x+1|-3,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

- $x\in (-\infty ,1]$
- $x\in [1,\infty )$
- $x\in (-\infty ,-1]$
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph of the function $f(x)=|x+1|-3$ can be obtained in the following way:

- Take the curve $y=|x|.$

- Translate it by $1$ units to the left,  to get $y=|x+1|.$

- Finally, translate $y=|x+1|$ by $3$ units down to get $f(x)=|x+1|-3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/3b9f56280089991c7db7652d84a777edd5c5e012921f0d48362f4fc3e4fd2a6e.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on each of the intervals $x\in (-\infty ,-1]$ and $x\in [1,\infty ).$ On these intervals, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/fd0b0fe70e009f43e80b0f712b6cfd576deb4c4c0457f61adae04cf7e44f140c.png)

  

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on the interval $x\in (-\infty ,1].$ On this interval, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/582ec1960b053731bf201c84d8c58fd4e1734a2b085cd5549a01aace4b600b4a.png)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only".
